title: Lowe’s helps CreatiVets build veteran arts and music center
summary: Lowe’s helps CreatiVets build veteran arts and music center
body_markdown:
Inside a former church,


CreatiVets


is building a 24-hour art and music center. Here, veterans will have the freedom to explore music, ceramics, woodworking, metalworking, and more whenever inspiration strikes.


A $350,000 Lowe’s Community Impact Grant is helping turn that vision into reality. The support, though, goes far beyond a check.


“Lowe’s came in big. We received $350,000 from Lowe’s for their community grant and it was game-changing,” Casper said. “A lot of people just see that dollar amount and they’re like, ‘Oh, that’s cool that they brought that.’ But no, they’re bringing hundreds of people here to do a lot more work on this space that we would’ve had to pay for.”


Recently, Lowe’s red vest associates gathered for a Red Vest Day at the center, lending hands and heart to refresh the space and bring opening day a little closer.


For James Dragon, a veteran and Lowe’s associate who knows his way around a wood shop, this project holds special meaning. With two wood shops planned for the new center, there’s hope this is just the start of something lasting.


“To be re-involved with the military, especially this project, is huge in my life,” Dragon said. “I was meant to be here.”
